$comment: GENERATED by scripts/build-service-bundle.mjs from the console fixtures. Loaded by engines/kotlin :service and planes/execution. Do not edit by hand.

offers.name: 5G Home Ultimate
offers.description: Fixed-wireless home internet where 5G coverage is strong.

offers.name: Disney Plus
offers.description: Partner streaming bundle, three months promotional.

offers.name: FIOS Gigabit
offers.description: Full-fiber gigabit internet, where the address can take it.

offers.name: Gaming Plus Bundle
offers.description: Low-latency router and gaming add-on for an existing line.

targetingPolicies.name: Bandwidth need in the usage profile
targetingPolicies.description: Offer the bigger pipe to the households using the one they have.

targetingPolicies.name: 5G Home coverage is strong
targetingPolicies.description: Fixed wireless needs strong coverage at the service address, not merely a signal.

targetingPolicies.name: Active account
targetingPolicies.description: Every offer in the brief requires an active consumer account.

targetingPolicies.name: Broadband need already met
targetingPolicies.description: Entertainment is a cross-sell onto a working line. This rule opens the category once broadband is provisioned, and it is why the follow-up interaction shows gaming and streaming rather than another broadband offer.

targetingPolicies.name: Disney+ partner bundle available in region
targetingPolicies.description: A partner bundle can only be sold where the agreement covers the region.

targetingPolicies.name: Entertainment affinity above threshold
targetingPolicies.description: The category gate: do not push streaming at a household that shows no interest in it.

targetingPolicies.name: Digital engagement or broadband intent
targetingPolicies.description: One field, not two conditions: the brief asks for digital engagement OR a broadband intent signal, and a policy ANDs its conditions. The disjunction is computed in the profile and named so a reader can see which question it answers.

targetingPolicies.name: Fiber serviceable at the address
targetingPolicies.description: Do not offer fiber where it cannot be installed. The value arrives from conn_serviceability, so a refusal can name the system that supplied the evidence.

targetingPolicies.name: Gaming affinity
targetingPolicies.description: Gaming Plus asks for more than a general interest in entertainment.

targetingPolicies.name: Broadband service on the account
targetingPolicies.description: Gaming Plus is an add-on to a line. Without the line there is nothing to add it to.

targetingPolicies.name: Netflix partner bundle available in region
targetingPolicies.description: A partner bundle can only be sold where the agreement covers the region.

targetingPolicies.name: No open broadband order
targetingPolicies.description: A line already being provisioned is not a line to sell again.

targetingPolicies.name: Not moving within 30 days
targetingPolicies.description: A line sold into an address they are leaving is a line that will be cancelled.

targetingPolicies.name: No existing 5G Home subscription
targetingPolicies.description: They already hold it. This is also what suppresses it after acceptance.

targetingPolicies.name: Not already subscribed to Disney+
targetingPolicies.description: Do not sell a bundle they already have.

targetingPolicies.name: Not already on FIOS
targetingPolicies.description: They already hold it. This is also what suppresses it after acceptance.

targetingPolicies.name: Not already subscribed to Netflix
targetingPolicies.description: Do not sell a bundle they already have.

frequencyPolicies.name: Email weekly cap
frequencyPolicies.description: At most two marketing emails a week, and a 30-day rest after a decline.

frequencyPolicies.name: Web session cap
frequencyPolicies.description: At most three decisioned slots a day on the web, and a 30-day rest on any offer the customer declines.

boosts.name: Fiber first where the address supports it
boosts.reason: Fiber leads where the address can take it. Authored for this demo by the product owner to break the three-way tie at business value 100: the customer has supplied no business-value ranking of their own, and the brief carries that order on an adaptive model this platform does not have.

boosts.name: The line before the add-on
boosts.reason: A broadband line outranks an add-on that attaches to one: selling the line is what makes the add-on possible, and a household with no internet cannot use a gaming bundle. Authored for this demo by the product owner to break the second tie at business value 100 — 5G Home Ultimate and Gaming Plus Bundle were level, and the engine was settling it by sorting keys alphabetically, which is an accident rather than a decision. In the no-fiber scenario that accident decided the headline slot.

connectors.name: Billing ledger
connectors.description: Current balance, arrears and rolling spend, pre-computed nightly and served from the online store.

connectors.name: Consent registry
connectors.description: Marketing and profiling consent of record. Defaults closed on failure, because assuming consent is the one mistake with a regulator attached.

connectors.name: Credit bureau
connectors.description: Full bureau file. Configured, and deliberately not wired into any live flow: at 180ms it cannot be called synchronously inside a 50ms budget, and the compiler says so rather than letting it fail in production.

connectors.name: Device catalogue
connectors.description: Handset stock and lead times. Not yet activated pending contract sign-off.

connectors.name: Engagement and partner availability
connectors.description: Category affinities, and which partner streaming agreements cover this region. Affinity is a computed score rather than a model output: it is read here, not predicted.

connectors.name: Network usage
connectors.description: Rolling 30-day data usage and account tenure from the mediation platform.

connectors.name: Order book
connectors.description: Whether a broadband order is already open on the account. A line being provisioned is not a line to sell again, and this is what makes the difference visible to a policy.

connectors.name: Address serviceability
connectors.description: What the network can deliver at a service address: whether fiber can be installed, and how strong 5G Home coverage is. The customer brief turns on this answer — a fiber address and a non-fiber address are the same visitor with one field different, and this is the field.

placements.name: Homepage hero
placements.description: The full-width banner above the fold. One action, unauthenticated traffic.

placements.name: Homepage grid
placements.description: Three cards below the hero. The slot that needs a slate rather than a winner.

placements.name: Account dashboard hero
placements.description: The signed-in dashboard banner. One action, and the customer is known.

placements.name: Usage page inline
placements.description: A single cross-sell strip under the usage meter.

placements.name: Weekly offers email
placements.description: The weekly send. Decided here; delivered by nothing yet — the outbound adapter is W-017.

placements.name: Triggered SMS
placements.description: A single message on a trigger — usage threshold, contract date, network event.

placements.name: App inbox
placements.description: The message list inside the app. Two slots, and the customer is known.

placements.name: Basket upsell (paused)
placements.description: A strip in the checkout basket. Switched off after the January test; the slot is kept so the history reads.

entities.name: Customer
entities.description: The person a decision is being made for, and what is known about them.

fields.name: age
fields.description: Age in whole years.

fields.name: credit_status
fields.description: Outcome of the internal credit check. Superseded for eligibility by the bureau band, which a connector supplies; kept because it is what the tenant records against the account.

fields.name: moving_within_days
fields.description: Days until a known house move, or a large number when none is known. A line sold into an address they are leaving is a line that will be cancelled.

fields.name: account_status
fields.description: Standing of the account.

fields.name: current_plan
fields.description: The plan they are on now. `none` for a prospect.

fields.name: bill_to_income_ratio
fields.description: Monthly bill as a share of income. The affordability input.

fields.name: arrears_count_12mo
fields.description: Arrears events in the last twelve months.

fields.name: monthly_spend
fields.description: Rolling monthly spend, from the billing ledger.

fields.name: arrears_days
fields.description: Days currently in arrears. 0 when in good standing.

fields.name: in_good_standing
fields.description: Whether the billing ledger considers the account current.

fields.name: tenure_months
fields.description: How long the customer has been with us.

fields.name: marketing_consent
fields.description: Marketing consent as the registry holds it. Distinct from what a caller asserts on the request, which ADR-014 §7 makes narrow-only.

fields.name: profiling_consent
fields.description: Consent to profiling, from the registry.

fields.name: credit_score
fields.description: Bureau score.

fields.name: credit_band
fields.description: Bureau band, A best. No targeting policy in this tenant reads it, so the bureau connector is a declaration rather than part of a decision — the flow’s source node does not call it. Not `required`: intake reads that flag as "this ingestion file must map it", and no file supplies this — the bureau does.

relationships.name: broadband
relationships.description: The internet service on the account.

relationships.name: engagement
relationships.description: Recent behaviour, reduced to what a policy asks.

relationships.name: accounts
relationships.description: Every account held. Nothing populates this yet — see docs/gaps.md.

entities.name: Context
entities.description: What only the caller can know about this request. Never stored: a decision reads it and it is gone.

fields.name: device_in_stock
fields.description: Whether the device can be supplied now. Under the request rather than the subject: it is a fact about this moment, not about a person.

relationships.name: offer
relationships.description: Facts about the offer being considered.

entities.name: Account
entities.description: One account held by a customer. Declared so the model can express a parent-child rollup; no source populates it yet.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Standing of this account.

fields.name: arrears_days
fields.description: Days this account is in arrears.

fields.name: balance
fields.description: Outstanding balance.

entities.name: Address
entities.description: The service address, and what the network can deliver there.

fields.name: fios_serviceable
fields.description: Whether full-fiber FIOS can be installed at this address.

fields.name: fiveg_coverage
fields.description: Measured 5G Home coverage at the address: strong, marginal or none. Fixed wireless needs strong, not merely a signal.

entities.name: Broadband
entities.description: The internet service on the account, if there is one.

fields.name: status
fields.description: active, ordered or none. "active" is what an add-on attaches to.

fields.name: product
fields.description: Which internet product they hold: fios, 5g_home, dsl or none. This is what stops an accepted offer being offered again.

entities.name: Orders
entities.description: Work already in flight, so a line being provisioned is not sold twice.

fields.name: open_broadband
fields.description: Whether a broadband order is already open on this account.

entities.name: Ott
entities.description: Partner streaming: what they hold, and what may be sold to them here.

fields.name: disney
fields.description: Already subscribed to the Disney+ bundle.

fields.name: netflix
fields.description: Already subscribed to the Netflix bundle.

fields.name: disney_available
fields.description: Whether the Disney+ partner agreement covers this region.

fields.name: netflix_available
fields.description: Whether the Netflix partner agreement covers this region.

entities.name: Affinity
entities.description: How interested this household looks, per category.

fields.name: gaming
fields.description: Gaming affinity, 0 to 1. Gaming Plus asks 0.5 or better.

fields.name: entertainment
fields.description: Entertainment affinity, 0 to 1. The category gate asks 0.5 or better.

entities.name: Engagement
entities.description: What they have been doing, reduced to the questions a policy asks.

fields.name: digital_or_broadband_intent
fields.description: True when there is digital engagement OR a broadband intent signal. One field because a policy ANDs its conditions and the brief asks for a disjunction — the OR is computed here, where it can be named, rather than approximated by two rules that would both have to pass.

entities.name: Usage
entities.description: Recent consumption, as a share of what was bought.

fields.name: pct_of_allowance_3mo_avg
fields.description: Mean share of the data allowance used over three months.

fields.name: months_of_history
fields.description: How many months of usage exist. A low value makes the average unreliable.

fields.name: data_usage_gb
fields.description: Data used in the current period.

fields.name: roaming_days
fields.description: Days roaming in the last period.

fields.name: days_to_end
fields.description: Days until the minimum term ends.

fields.name: pac_requested_within_days
fields.description: Days since a porting code was requested. A large value means never.

fields.name: residual_value
fields.description: What the device is still worth.

entities.name: OfferContext
entities.description: Facts about the offer under consideration, supplied per decision. Not the offer catalogue — this is what changes for this customer.

fields.name: monthly_delta
fields.description: Change to the monthly bill if accepted. Negative is a saving. One value for the whole request: the schema has no per-candidate scope, which ADR-014 §2 records. The suitability policy that assumed otherwise went with the telco-uk catalogue; this tenant declares no suitability policies at all.

entities.name: Offer
entities.description: The offer being judged, read once per candidate from its record in the catalogue. Not OfferContext, which is one value the caller sends for the whole request.

fields.name: boost
fields.description: The offer’s own business boost. 1.0 is neutral.

entities.name: OfferFinancials
entities.description: What the offer costs the customer and what it earns.

fields.name: termMonths
fields.description: Commitment length. 0 means no commitment.

relationships.name: price
relationships.description: What the customer pays, per month unless one-off.

relationships.name: cost
relationships.description: Cost to serve, over the same period as the price.

relationships.name: expectedMargin
relationships.description: Expected margin per accepted offer over the term.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: In minor units, the same unit as customer.monthly_spend.

aggregations.description: The worst arrears across every account held. Declared to fix the shape of a rollup before anything depends on it; nothing resolves it yet.
How many accounts are currently active.

experiments.name: FIOS Gigabit holdout
experiments.description: One in ten customers is held back from FIOS Gigabit, so the uplift can be measured against people who were eligible and never asked.

experiments.name: Homepage hero wording
experiments.description: Two headlines for the homepage hero. Stopped; kept because the decisions it influenced are still in the ledger and still have to be explainable.
